scenarios.value:
AV:N - An unauthenticated peer supplies IPv4 Record Route or Timestamp bytes in a TCP SYN; ip_rcv_options() and tcp_v4_save_options() store them in ireq_opt. Its retransmitted SYN follows tcp_v4_rcv()->tcp_check_req()->tcp_rtx_synack()->tcp_v4_send_synack(), racing frees in patched inet_sock_destruct() or tcp_v4_reqsk_destructor().
AC:L - On an accepting server, the peer can repeatedly create an option-bearing request and race a retransmitted SYN against completing and tearing down that same TCP connection. Both racing sides are attacker-induced; multicore scheduling and heap grooming do not constitute conditions outside the attacker's influence.
PR:N - tcp_v4_rcv() reaches tcp_check_req() and tcp_v4_send_synack() during the TCP handshake, before application authentication. The target performs no capability or credential check on the peer's valid IPv4 Record Route or Timestamp option.
UI:N - The peer sends the option-bearing SYN, retransmitted SYN, and handshake or teardown packets to an already listening service; no victim user must mount, open, or approve anything.
S:U - The stale ip_options_rcu object is consumed and corrupts memory within the same host kernel in ip_build_and_send_pkt() and ip_options_build(); no separate security authority is crossed.
C:H - After inet_sock_destruct() frees inet_opt, ip_options_build() copies opt->__data for the stale opt->optlen into the network-bound SYNACK. Reclaiming the object can therefore disclose adjacent kernel heap contents directly to the peer.
I:H - Reclaiming the freed ip_options_rcu lets stale optlen and srr, rr, or ts offsets steer ip_options_build() memcpy and address or timestamp writes, permitting out-of-bounds kernel writes and potential control-flow corruption.
A:H - A reclaimed optlen can make ip_build_and_send_pkt() call skb_push() beyond the SYNACK headroom, invoking skb_under_panic(); the stale-offset writes in ip_options_build() can also oops the kernel.
